title: Capacity-aware routing & admission control — notes
body:
Context:

Quick working notes for a capacity-aware routing + admission-control design that needs to gate traffic to GPU pools while preserving SLOs across regions and customer tiers. This doc is intentionally high-iteration: sketches, heuristics, and concrete config knobs we can spike. Aim: protect model serving from long tails and overloaded nodes while allowing predictable bursts for paying customers.

Goals / constraints:
- Maintain 99th percentile latency SLOs for latency-sensitive routes (chat/generation) while maximizing throughput.
- Avoid cascading retries across the control plane and client side (reduce retry storms).
- Support multi-region deployments + graceful cross-region fallback when local capacity constrained.
- Allow prioritized burst allocation for premium tenants without starving best-effort workloads.
- Provide telemetry that ties rejections/throttles to capacity signals (GPU utilization, queue depth, instance health).

Assumptions:
- Each GPU server exposes: current GPU util %, queue_depth (number of inflight requests or pending batches), per-model token-cost estimate (tokens/sec or tokens/request), and a health flag.
- Serving runtime provides a cheap estimate for request token-cost at admission time (or default per model).
- Control plane has eventual visibility of instance-level metrics with ~2-5s lag for aggregates; faster local agents can make immediate decisions.
- We keep per-tenant/account and per-route config (priority, burst quota, steady quota).

Signals to use for admission decisions:
- Token-bucket remaining capacity (per-tenant, per-route, and global per-cluster).
- Queue depth per-node and p50/p95 queue depth observed across pool.
- GPU utilization (smoothed EWMA over 10s and 60s windows) and per-GPU memory headroom.
- Recent reject rate and latency tail (to detect overload before saturating).
- Autoscaler state (scaling_in_progress, current_target_replicas) to avoid oscillation.

Admission decision primitives (terminology):
- ACCEPT: route to chosen node; enqueue for immediate batching.
- DEFER: queue at edge/proxy for short backoff (e.g., 50–200ms) hoping queue clears (only if local queue_depth < hard limit).
- THROTTLE: accept but reduce request size/compute (e.g., force quantized model variant, lower max tokens) — mid-tier fallback.
- REJECT (429): immediate rejection for non-critical or when fair-share exhausted.
- FALLBACK-REGION: reroute to a different region/pool with available capacity (policy-driven).

Design sketch: hybrid token-bucket + dynamic headroom gating

1) Per-tenant token buckets (control-plane enforced):
- Each tenant has two logical buckets: steady_rate and burst_bucket.
- steady_rate replenishes at R tokens/sec (tokens here are not literal tokens; unit = estimated model-token-cost per request; normalized to "compute units").
- burst_bucket allows short bursts up to B units and refills more slowly (multi-minute).
- When a request arrives, we estimate compute_cost C. Admission first consumes steady_rate; if insufficient and burst_bucket > C and request priority allows bursts, consume burst. If both insufficient -> move to next step (defer/reject).

2) Node-level headroom check (local agent):
- Local agent computes headroom H = f(1 - normalized_gpu_util, free_memory_fraction, 1/(1+queue_depth)). Normalize to 0..1.
- If headroom < threshold T_accept (e.g., 0.25), local agent signals temporary hard-reject for new tokens that would increase tail. If headroom between T_defer and T_accept (e.g., 0.25–0.5), return DEFER suggestion to edge (small queuing). If headroom > T_defer, ACCEPT.

3) Queue-depth safeguards:
- Each node has two queue thresholds: q_soft and q_hard. Past q_soft, start returning DEFER to encourage client-side queuing. Past q_hard -> REJECT.
- Backpressure windows: once node hits q_hard, enter a cooldown where node accepts only critical traffic for S seconds.

4) Multi-region fallback policy:
- Control plane maintains per-region spare capacity estimate (aggregated headroom across pool) and a cost multiplier (latency penalty + egress cost).
- If local admission fails but tenant has cross-region allowed flag and cost-budget, attempt FALLBACK-REGION to region with spare capacity and acceptable latency.
- Rate limit cross-region fallbacks to avoid moving entire workload to another region (circuit-breaker by region).

5) Priority & fairness rules:
- Assign classes: critical (SLA-backed), standard (paid), best-effort (free/experiment).
- Critical traffic can borrow burst_bucket up to B_crit and preempt best-effort requests (best-effort gets preemptible tokens). Preemption implemented at enqueuing time (drop or deprioritize best-effort batches if memory needed).
- Fair-share pool: a global token bucket that prevents any single tenant from consuming >X% of cluster steady capacity for prolonged periods.

6) Autoscaler & admission interplay:
- Autoscaler should expose a predicted capacity delta over next minute. Admission should be more conservative while scaling_up=false and node headroom trending down.
- When autoscaler is scaling up, temporarily raise steady_rate caps gradually to soak new capacity (avoid instant overload).

7) Observability and tracing needs:
- Tag every admission decision with: reason (token-bucket / headroom / queue_depth / policy), consumed_buckets (steady/burst/global), node_id, region, and estimated_cost.
- Emit metrics: admission_accept_rate, defer_rate, reject_rate, fallback_rate, avg_headroom_by_region, per-tenant_burst_spend, preemptions_count.
- Create an alert: if reject_rate > 0.5% and system headroom < 20% -> paging.

8) Config knobs for rollout and experiments:
- T_accept, T_defer, q_soft, q_hard, burst sizes (B per tier), per-tenant steady R, multi-region circuit-breaker thresholds, preemption_enabled.
- Start with conservative thresholds in prod: T_accept=0.3, T_defer=0.5, q_soft=16, q_hard=48. Iterate after canary.

Admission pseudocode (edge view):
- on_request(req):
-   C = estimate_cost(req)
-   if not control_plane.check_tenant_quota(req.tenant, C):
-       return REJECT(429, reason=quota)
-   node_hint = pick_node_hint(req.route)
-   node_decision = node_hint.local_agent.can_accept(C)
-   if node_decision == ACCEPT: forward
-   if node_decision == DEFER: enqueue_short_wait_or_retry(50-200ms window)
-   if node_decision == REJECT: if req.allows_fallback then try_fallback_region(req) else return REJECT

Open questions / risks:
- How accurate are cost estimates? For chat + streaming, token estimation is tricky. We should add a conservative multiplier for streaming requests.
- Cross-region fallbacks increase egress cost and latency — need explicit billing guardrails and per-tenant policy.
- Risk of burst_bucket exhaustion causing repeated 429s for high-throughput tenants; need graceful degradation ( degrade model quality instead of rejecting when possible ).

Plan / next steps:
- Spike: implement a local agent that exposes headroom and queue thresholds (2 engineers, 2-week spike).
- Telemetry: wire admission decision tags into tracing and Prometheus metrics (1 week).
- Experiment: enable per-tenant steady+burst buckets in canary region and observe 95/99 latency and reject rates (2 weeks).
- Policy: product and billing to define cross-region fallback pricing and customer opt-in.

Action items:
- Priya: draft node local_agent API spec + proto of headroom signal (due 2026-03-05) — DONE (see linked PR)
- Ethan: prototype edge logic for token-bucket + defer loop (2026-03-03)
- Maya: telemetry dashboard template for admission metrics (2026-03-08)
- Jonah: run load tests with synthetic long-tail requests to validate q_soft/q_hard settings (2026-03-12)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider moving from hard token-buckets to leaky-bucket variant with adaptive refill when average utilization < target.
- For GPU memory-limited models, admission should also account for per-model memory footprint and prefer routing compact quantized variants when memory pressure high.
- Keep operator controls to temporarily disable preemption for specific tenants when debugging incidents.

References / inspiration:
- Netflix Zuul / Hystrix (circuit-breaker and fallback patterns)
- Google Borg's locality-aware scheduling heuristics
- Prior art: Istio request-level circuit breakers + k8s HorizontalPodAutoscaler interplay.

End of notes. Feedback welcome — especially on token cost normalization approach and cross-region fallback guardrails.
